_note: Every muscle string the upstream dataset carries in `target`, `muscle_group`
and `secondary_muscles`, mapped onto the canonical enum (§5.4). This is the
one table — no other normalisation happens anywhere in the pipeline.
`map` is a complete census of the 49 distinct strings in the 1,295 non-cardio
records at SOURCE_COMMIT. Any string absent from it fails the build and is
written to unmapped.json; silent pass-through is what lets synonym drift reach
the database, so there is no fallback.
Two members were added to §5.4's list in M2, with the owner's agreement:
`delts` — the dataset never distinguishes the three heads. `delts`,
`deltoids` and `shoulders` are one undifferentiated bucket upstream
(777 mentions), and splitting them by guesswork would put wrong numbers
in M6's per-muscle volume. `front_delts` and `side_delts` therefore never
appear from this table at all — they only arrive through the
hand-maintained delt_heads.json override. `rear_delts` is the exception:
upstream does say `rear deltoids`, in secondary lists only.
`other` — the long tail that has no honest home in the enum: rotator cuff,
ankles, feet, shins, ankle stabilizers, serratus anterior. 49 mentions
between them, almost all secondary. Better one visibly-unclassified bucket
than six muscles filed under near neighbours.

_judgement_calls.back: Generic, 11 secondary mentions only. Filed under upper_back rather than lats because the records using it are rows and carries, not pulldowns.
_judgement_calls.spine: 19 target mentions, all hyperextensions and back extensions. lower_back is what the movement actually trains.
_judgement_calls.serratus anterior: 5 target mentions. Genuinely not chest and not core; left visible under `other` rather than absorbed into either.
_judgement_calls.rotator cuff: 10 mentions → rear_delts (owner's call, M2). The exercises using it are face pulls and external rotations, which are rear-delt work in any training sense. Filing them under `other` would make M6 undercount rear delts — the area a Push/Pull/Legs split is most likely to be short on, and the one the owner is most likely to be asking the volume summary about. The anatomical objection (the cuff is four muscles, none of them the deltoid) loses to the practical one: these sets are counted somewhere, and rear_delts is where a lifter would look for them.
_judgement_calls.grip muscles / hands / wrists: All forearms. The distinction is anatomical, not a training-volume one.
